discovery.root: GET / redirects to /login (welcome). This catalog is served at GET /discovery.
discovery.register_page: GET /register → /login?join=1; GET /login?resend=1 opens resend card; fragments under shared UI-card limit
discovery.home_page: GET /home (signed-in shell: profile-completion gate or feed + rail; HTML); GET /onboarding (onboarding workflow shell: face capture + godmother); GET /home/profile-completion-card (onboarding — human profile); GET|POST /home/judicial/post/{post_id} (file post-scoped judicial_case); GET|POST /home/judicial/post/{post_id}/appeal (appeal resolved post_moderation case to AI council; ?from_case=); POST /me/reverse-geocode (optional country default); POST /me/google-place-location (Place ID → Google validate → update human entity location); POST /me/human-profile (save profile); POST /me/face-capture (multipart: embedding + three JPEGs named neutral, smile, frown; mock mode or gRPC AI gateway)
discovery.locations: POST /locations (verified session + JSON body; rate limited)
discovery.ops_invalidate: POST /ops/locations/invalidate (Bearer OPS_LOCATION_INVALIDATE_TOKEN; not session-auth; 404 if token unset)
discovery.ops_jobs_run: POST /ops/jobs/run (Bearer OPS_JOB_QUEUE_TOKEN; JSON body optional batch_size; conductor: archive TTL, lease reap, fair claim, run handlers; 404 if token unset)
discovery.jobs: POST /jobs/enqueue (verified session JSON { job_type_key, payload, optional priority }); POST /jobs/{id}/cancel (pending only); dedupe by SHA-256 of canonical JSON per job type
discovery.ref_key_values: GET /ref-key-values?group= (active rows; rate limited). Group verification_tier is internal-only and rejected.
discovery.social_entities: POST /social-entities (handle + …), GET /social-entities/{id} (verified session; POST rate limited)
discovery.face_capture: GET /onboarding (verified session; onboarding workflow shell); POST /me/face-capture (multipart; mock or gRPC AI gateway; rate limited)
discovery.entity_public_profile: GET /public/{handle} (HTML shell) + GET /api/public/entity-profile/{handle} (public JSON card; no auth; verified entities only; shared rate limit)

auth.me_human_profile: POST /me/human-profile (verified session; first human + location + social_human)

login.constitution_intro: Root-level principles from the 256 Operating Charter (16 points) — inherited by every community on the network.
login.constitution_item_1: The Principle of Voluntary Association — Every community is an opt-in collective. No human shall be bound to a community without explicit consent, except the Root itself, which constitutes the shared reality of the Network.
login.constitution_item_2: The Right of Exit — The path of departure shall remain as frictionless as the path of entry. Any human may leave a community; any community may migrate or dissolve, subject to its governance quorums. Exit shall not be penalized by retroactive standing loss for past lawful participation.
login.constitution_item_3: The Integrity of the Vote — The ballot is sacrosanct. Spoofing, botting, or bypassing sortition mechanisms strikes at the Root. The AI Council exists to protect the vote, not the voter.
login.constitution_item_4: Universal Safety Floor — The Network prohibits content and conduct that universally endangers people: child sexual abuse material and exploitation of minors; credible threats of physical violence; non-consensual intimate imagery; doxxing; fraud, scams, and impersonation intended to harm; coordinated harassment and bullying as conduct; and distribution of malware or phishing intended to harm. Lawful protected identity and belief (item 7) are not violations here solely because they are illegal or stigmatized elsewhere. This point defines what is forbidden; routing is under Acute Harm Sanitation (15), Legal Process (11), or Civic Moderation (13). Select §4.1–§4.7 when filing emergency safety reports.
login.constitution_item_5: The Privacy of Weight — Every human has the right to know their own social standing and the variables that affect it. No other participant may see another human's standing or vote weight.
login.constitution_item_6: The Finality of Challenge — No constitutional verdict is beyond review until it reaches the AI Council on permitted civic moderation appeals under point 13. Council jurisdiction is appellate and interpretive — not legislative, not constitutional amendment, and not acute harm sanitation under point 15.
login.constitution_item_7: Cognitive Liberty and Protected Identity — The Network shall not mandate internal thought, only external conduct. Communities may define topic relevance in their own clauses; they may not prohibit protected identity or belief. Sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, ethnicity, religion, and non-belief are protected. Locale law or custom is not grounds to remove lawful identity expression that does not otherwise violate the Universal Safety Floor (item 4).
login.constitution_item_8: The Duty of Participation — Citizenship is a function of participation. Prolonged absence may reduce standing under published rules, distinguished from persistent unfitness under point 12.
login.constitution_item_9: Preservation of the Tree — No community rule may override a Root principle. Precedence: Universal Safety Floor (4) → Acute Harm Sanitation (15) and Mandatory Reporting (16) → Voluntary Association, Right of Exit, Protected Identity (1, 2, 7) → Legal Process (11) → Civic Moderation and Dignity in Process (13, 14) → standing and governance machinery (5, 6, 10) → community-owned clauses → cross-border visibility within point 11. Foundational seed communities may carry structural immunity from fitness extinction, but not immunity from points 4, 11, 15, or 16.
login.constitution_item_10: Financial Accountability — Every token earned or spent in governance shall be traceable to its agency or community of origin.
login.constitution_item_11: Legal Process and Cross-Border Visibility — The Network cooperates with valid legal process where the operator has legal duty or nexus. Lawful authority requests are handled by the operator, not by civic juries. The operator maintains preservation procedures without requiring jurors to review material routed under Acute Harm Sanitation (15). When content is lawful under Root principles in its community context but restricted elsewhere, the Network may limit visibility by geography rather than require global removal. Not selectable as a civic moderation violation clause.
login.constitution_item_12: Sunset and Renewal — Stagnation is unfitness. Communities that fail to govern or evolve may be returned to the parent node. Local extinction shall preserve descendant communities where the tree allows. Fitness consequences shall be proportionate and reversible where rehabilitation is possible.
login.constitution_item_13: Civic Moderation Process — Constitutional disagreement is resolved through post dispute among the post audience. In scope: community norms and non-acute Safety Floor disputes. Out of scope: CSAM and machine-first sanitation matches (15); operator legal process (11) and mandatory reporting (16). Emergency safety under §4.1–§4.7 follows a separate suppress-first path until the author contests. Civic moderation is not an emergency service.
login.constitution_item_14: Dignity in Civic Process — Filing cases, jury service, and appeals must not harass, brigade, retaliate, or re-traumatize participants. Bad-faith filing — including citing the Safety Floor to bypass civic rules or target protected identity (item 7) — violates this principle. When a jury clears the post, the filer receives an automatic fitness penalty at resolution.
login.constitution_item_15: Acute Harm Sanitation — Certain harms require immediate containment and machine-first handling. No participant, juror, council member, or operator shall be required to view CSAM or non-consensual intimate imagery in raw form. Class A/B media is blocked before persistence and never enters civic moderation or council corpora. Class C imminent threats and active doxxing are hidden immediately for operator response. Known malware and phishing domains are blocked at link ingest. Every sanitation action produces an audit record.
login.constitution_item_16: Mandatory Reporting and External Duty — Where the operator has legal duty or participates in recognized global reporting programs, the Network reports, refers, or preserves through designated channels — not through ad hoc law-enforcement contact by participants or jurors. CSAM and exploitation are reported through applicable hotlines. Imminent threat to life: preserve evidence and direct users to local emergency services. Self-harm crisis: the Network surfaces crisis resources; jury service is not crisis intervention.

legal.terms_body:
These Terms & Conditions govern your use of 256.app (the Network). By creating an account or continuing to use the service, you agree to them and to the 256 Root Operating Charter in effect at signup (currently version v2-2026-05-29).

Eligibility: you must be 16 or older. Registration requires a verified email, a password, explicit consent to the Root Charter, and confirmation that you meet the age requirement.

The Network is a link-and-text social product: we do not host user-uploaded photos, videos, or arbitrary file attachments on posts or profiles. Discussion happens in text and attached outbound links (with OG previews where available). The only stored portrait is your generated council-style avatar from onboarding face capture.

Conduct, safety, and disputes are governed by the Root Charter, including the Universal Safety Floor, emergency safety sanitation, civic moderation among the post audience, dignity in civic process, and operator legal process where applicable. Community rules cannot override Root principles.

Noms are in-app credits spent on platform actions such as judicial filings and AI services; you receive a starter grant at signup and may buy more via Stripe. They are not cash currency.

We may update these terms or the charter; material changes are reflected in the consent version recorded on your account. Continued use after notice constitutes acceptance where permitted by law.
legal.privacy_body:
256.app is built to collect the minimum data needed to run a human-centred community.

We do not store images you upload to posts or profiles. Onboarding face capture is transient: we do not keep raw photos or biometric embeddings—only a generated avatar image and a completion flag. Posts are text and optional outbound links; link previews fetch public metadata only.

We do not sell your personal data to third parties. The home feed has no third-party advertising.

For location we store country-level association on your profile (ISO country code), not a street address collected by us by default. Account data includes your email for sign-in and verification and fields you choose to publish on your profile.

Operators may process safety reports and legal requests under the Root Charter. See Safety & Crisis for tiered response and crisis hotlines.
legal.safety_body:
256.app uses tiered responses for harm, disputes, and crisis support.

• Tier 1 — acute harm (minutes): operator action for CSAM, credible imminent violence, and active doxxing with a safety nexus; mandatory external reporting under Root point 16 where legally required.
• Tier 2 — platform policy (hours): report flows, link denylist, and acute harm sanitation (Root point 15), including hash gates. Class A/B imagery never enters civic juries or council review — it applies to avatar and logo ingress only, not link-card previews.
• Tier 2b — outbound links: known-bad domains are blocked at attach; URLs in post text are checked against the same blocklist; preview images from new or unestablished domains stay hidden until you tap Show preview (title and hostname still show).
• Tier 3 — civic moderation (days): human juries among the post audience for constitutional disagreement (Root point 13).
• Emergency safety (§4.2, §4.4): a post is suppressed immediately; the author may contest (1 Nom) to open a jury.
• Sanitation-only (§4.1, §4.3, §4.7): not jury paths.
• Legal process (Root point 11): operator-handled, not a dispute you file to a jury.
• Closed beta on-call: for acute platform safety (not jury timelines), email {safety_contact_email} — we aim to respond within 24 hours on business days; use emergency safety filing in-app when harm is immediate.
• Immediate danger: contact local emergency services. Jury timelines are not an emergency hotline — use the numbers below when you need crisis support.
• We do not file CyberTipline reports on your behalf — operators preserve logs and escalate manually where legally required.
legal.how_body:
256.app is a human-centred social platform built around meaningful connection, intentional communities, and civic governance.

Civics

Every community on 256.app is governed by its own constitution, rooted in the Root Operating Charter. When a post is disputed, a human jury of community members decides the outcome — not a single moderator or algorithm.

• Filing: any member may file a civic dispute against a post that violates the community's constitution (1 Nom). Emergency safety filings (also 1 Nom) hide a post immediately; the author may contest (1 Nom) to open a jury.
• Jury selection: jurors are drawn from the post's real audience — the community members, friends, or connections who would see it. Jury size follows the square-root rule (√n of the eligible pool), capped at 12 for post disputes.
• Vote weight: a juror's vote is weighted by their community standing on a 0–2 scale. A rating of 2.50 (the neutral default) gives a full vote weight of 1.0.
• Verdict: a two-thirds majority of weighted votes is required to uphold a case. Verdicts affect the standing of both the poster and the community.
• Appeals: resolved civic disputes can be escalated to the Council of 12 — a panel of AI advisors — for a second opinion (32 Noms).
• No jury: if a jury cannot be seated within 7 days (serious cases) or 21 days (civic cases), the post stays flagged and the community's rating is penalised.

Social graph

Each human profile supports up to 256 distinct active connections — the Dunbar-scale limit that keeps your network human and intentional. Communities, organisations, and AI entities have no connection cap.

Noms

Noms are the platform's internal currency for civic and AI actions — filing cases, contesting decisions, proposing constitutional amendments, and council-assisted services. You receive a starter grant at signup and may buy more when you need them. The feed is ad-free; Noms are acts of conscience, not a revenue lever from advertising.

[civic-standing] Civic standing

Your standing on 256.app has two layers: global standing (your reputation across the network) and per-community edge standing (how each community you belong to rates you as a member).

• Scale: 0.00 to 5.00 stars. New humans and communities start at 2.50 — a neutral floor, not a blank slate.
• Two layers: global standing (network-wide) and per-community edge standing on each active membership.
• What moves standing up: serving on a jury when a case you voted on resolves (+3 Noms and a standing bump); conversation settlement when a thread closes (Loved, Loathed, or Controversial outcomes apply different edge and global deltas); timely civic moderation that seats a jury.
• What moves standing down: civic or emergency verdicts against you; bad-faith filing when a jury clears the post or the author wins a contest (a substantial penalty for the filer); login inactivity after 28 days away (phased daily decrements — sign in to refund debited standing and reset the clock).
• Failing band: below 0.66 you are in the failing band. For humans, warnings appear on your own profile only — others do not see your numeric scores. Communities show public failing presentation.
• Zero: at 0.00 the entity is removed from the active graph (human death ritual or community death). Historical posts remain with dead-handle styling.
• Privacy: only you see your human global and edge scores. Other members see your membership and participation — not your numbers. This is how the platform honours self-knowledge (charter point 5) while keeping standing from becoming a public scoreboard.
